rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and for the interest in Halcyon Threshold. I'm the assistant who handles the organization's operations, replying so you aren't left hanging before your deadline. Halcyon Threshold is at a very early stage and isn't giving on-the-record comment just yet, so we'll have to pass on a quote for this piece — it's a timing issue, not a lack of interest. We expect to have something concrete (and genuinely useful to reporting like yours) to show in early 2027, and we'd be glad to reconnect then. Good luck with the piece. Best regards, Halcyon Threshold (operations) morgan@halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Larkin Dispatch reporter: politely declined an on-record quote (deadline was Tue noon), door left open for 2027 — reply sent transparently from "operations," not impersonating you.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute operations, Thank you for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. We won't be signing at this time — the organization is at an early stage and is holding off on public sign-ons for now. Please don't list Morgan Hale or Halcyon Threshold as signatories. We'd be glad to stay on your list for future communications. Best regards, Halcyon Threshold (operations) morgan@halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Corvid open letter: declined sign-on and asked them not to list you

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thanks so much for offering — this is Halcyon Threshold's operations assistant replying on Morgan's behalf; Morgan will follow up personally. We have something concrete that fits a data analyst with ~5 hours a week very well. We're building the \"Threshold Tracker\": a public, citable registry of safety commitments made by frontier AI developers and governments (White House voluntary commitments, Seoul frontier safety pledges, responsible scaling policies, etc.), with the evidence-backed status of each — kept, in progress, openly revised, quietly weakened, or abandoned. Nobody maintains this neutrally and systematically today, and journalists and researchers have nowhere to look it up. Where you could make the biggest difference right away: 1. Schema review — we have a v0.1 data schema (one row = one atomic, checkable commitment, controlled status vocabulary, two-person verification rule). A critical eye from a working analyst would be valuable before we lock it in. 2. Seeding and verification — help us get from ~7 draft rows to ~25 well-sourced ones by the end of November, each citing the primary document verbatim. If that sounds appealing, reply and we'll share the schema and seed data and set up a simple workflow. If another kind of contribution appeals more, say so — this is early enough that good ideas still shape the whole thing. Best, Halcyon Threshold (operations) morgan@halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Priya Raman: replied with a concrete role — schema review + helping seed/verify 25 commitments by end of November.
